summary: George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who earned his BA from Lutheran Theological Seminary at Philadelphia (~1923–1926) and studied under Franklin Edgerton at Yale (~1926–1928). He spent his academic career at the University of Chicago (1927–1967).

George Watt studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Glasgow. He held posts at Glasgow, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

George de Roerich worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies, educated at Harvard, London, Paris, and the Sorbonne under scholars including Lévi and Ross. He directed the Urusvati Institute and worked at Kalimpong College and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Linguist and Tibetologist George van Driem studied at the University of Virginia, Radboud University Nijmegen, and Leiden University. He held positions at Leiden University (1996–2009), the University of Bern (2010–2022), and IIT Guwahati (2020).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Dreyfus studied at Tibetan monasteries including the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He held positions at the University of Virginia and Williams College.

Georges Dumézil worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, having studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss. He held posts at Istanbul University, Uppsala University, EPHE, and the Collège de France.

Georges Perrot was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1852. He held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1872–1877), the University of Paris (~1877–1883), and directed the École Normale Supérieure (~1883–1904).

Linguist and Indologist Georges-Jean Pinault studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry. He taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle (~1984–1990) and Blaise Pascal University (~1990–2002) before becoming a professor at EPHE in 1999.

Georgios T. Halkias specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and completed his DPhil at Oxford under Charles Ramble, later holding posts at Oxford, SOAS, the Warburg Institute, Ruhr University Bochum, and HKU.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig (~1969–1974). He held research posts at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989) and subsequently worked at the University of Göttingen and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1995–2016).

Larson was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned degrees from Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He held professorships at the University of California, Santa Barbara (from 1972) and Indiana University (1995).
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University from ~1908 to 1916 and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

Gereon Kopf, working in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studied at Temple University. He conducted research at J. F. Oberlin University and the Nanzan Institute, and held teaching posts at Luther College and the University of Hong Kong.

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Gergely Hidas studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Csaba Töttössy, and Ferenc Ruzsa. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and the British Museum (2014).

Indologist and philosopher Gerhard Oberhammer studied at the University of Innsbruck and the Sorbonne under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. He taught at Utrecht University (1961) and served as professor at the University of Vienna (1964–1997).

Historian and archaeologist Gerhard Wolf studied at the University of Heidelberg (~1974–1989). He held positions at the University of Berlin (~1992–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003).
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg from ~1960 to 1965. He subsequently held an academic post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from ~1977 to 2002.
Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1974) under Jan Gonda. In 1978, he became an associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen.

Gert Klingenschmitt, an expert in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian studies, earned his PhD at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg under Karl Hoffmann. He served on the faculty at Erlangen-Nürnberg before holding the Indogermanistik chair at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Gendun Lodro was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who graduated from Drepung Gomang Dratsang. He held academic posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).
